rows.english: Here the great Tsongkapa is urging his readers to study the work: "You, you people who are seeking freedom and have no single moment's craving for the pleasures of life; you, who want to get the absolute most from the body you've found, to make your leisure and fortune meaningful; you now are going to have to train yourself in a path that never errs, a path that never strays, a path that is whole and complete, the path which pleases even the Buddhas--the one in the end they advise, a path that is no erring path, a path that is no path that strays, a path that is more than just some piece or part of a path. And if you want to train yourself in a path like that, you're going to have to be a student who has all the requirements of a student; you're going to have to fit the description from the 400 Verses:

rows.english: The "Independent" group has a way of describing interdependence that's a little bit better. They say that something is interdependent whenever it exists in dependence upon its parts. They then can establish interdependence with both changing and unchanging objects: for those with causes and without.

rows.acip: CHOS THAMS CAD CES GZUGS NAS RNAM MKHYEN GYI BAR GYI CHOS THAMS CAD RANG GI CHA SHAS LA BRTEN NAS GRUB PAS NA THA SNYAD DU RGYU 'BRAS BSLU BA MED PA DANG , DGAG BYA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I DMIGS GTAD ZHIG NAS BDEN PAR GRUB PA'AM, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I DNGOS PO CUNG ZAD TZAM YANG MED PAR RTOGS PA DE RGYAL BA DGYES PA'I LAM YIN,
rows.wylie: chos thams cad ces gzugs nas rnam mkhyen gyi bar gyi chos thams cad rang gi cha shas la brten nas grub pas na tha snyad du rgyu 'bras bslu ba med pa dang , dgag bya rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i dmigs gtad zhig nas bden par grub pa'am, rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i dngos po cung zad tsam yang med par rtogs pa de rgyal ba dgyes pa'i lam yin
rows.english: The expression "all objects" refers to each and every object from basic physical matter on up to the omniscience of a Buddha. They all exist in dependence upon their parts, so in a manner of speaking their "cause and effect can never fail." The antithesis, which we seek to disprove, is that these objects could have the solid existence they appear to have: that they could exist naturally. "When they lose all solid appearance"--that is, when we perceive that there is not a single thing in the universe which has any true or natural existence--then we have found "the path that pleases the Buddhas."

rows.acip: 'DOD PA'I RTEN CAN LA 'PHAGS PA SGUR CHUNG THAL SKYO GSOL NAS GRONGS PA DANG , 'PHAGS PA 'CHAR KA GZUGS 'TSONG MA'I GNAS SU DBU BCAD DE GRONGS PA DANG , RANG SANGS RGYAS DUG 'DAS BKRONGS PA DANG , SANGS RGYAS LA'ANG ZHABS LA SENG LDENG GI TSAL PA ZUG PA DANG , SKU RO RGYAB BSNYUNG BA DANG , LHAS SBYIN GYI 'KHRUL 'KHOR GYI SGYOGS KYI CHA SHAS PHOG PAS SKU MTSAL BYUNG BA LA SOGS PA SDUG BSNGAL GYI SDUG BSNGAL DANG BCAS PAR MDO LAS 'BYUNG BA'I PHYIR RO,
rows.wylie: 'dod pa'i rten can la 'phags pa sgur chung thal skyo gsol nas grongs pa dang , 'phags pa 'char ka gzugs 'tshong ma'i gnas su dbu bcad de grongs pa dang , rang sangs rgyas dug 'das bkrongs pa dang , sangs rgyas la'ang zhabs la seng ldeng gi tshal pa zug pa dang , sku ro rgyab bsnyung ba dang , lhas sbyin gyi 'khrul 'khor gyi sgyogs kyi cha shas phog pas sku mtshal byung ba la sogs pa sdug bsngal gyi sdug bsngal dang bcas par mdo las 'byung ba'i phyir ro
rows.english: We can see occurrences in sutra of persons who had attained this nirvana, who were living in desire-realm bodies and still had to go through outright suffering. Arya Gurchung, for example, was forced to consume a soup of water and ashes, which killed him. The Arya Udayin was decapitated in a brothel. We hear of a self-made Buddha who died from a wound inflicted by a poisoned arrow. Even the Buddha himself was pricked by the sandalwood thorn, suffered from backache, and bled where he was hit from the fragments of shells hurled by Devadatta's catapult.

rows.acip: ,'GREL PA DER CHAGS SOGS RNAMS THAG PA LA SBRUL DU BTAGS PA LTAR GSUNGS PA NI MTSON PA TZAM STE, CHOS GZHAN THAMS CAD KYANG THAG PA LA SBRUL DU BTAGS PA LTAR RTOG PAS BZHAG PAR 'CHAD PA'O, , DE LA KHRA BO'I MDOG DANG 'KHYIL LUGS SBRUL DANG 'DRA ZHING , YUL MI GSAL BAR SNANG BA NA THAG PA LA 'DI SBRUL LO SNYAM PA 'BYUNG NGO , , DE'I TSE THAG PA LA THAG PA'I TSOGS PA DANG CHA SHAS SBRUL GYI MTSAN GZHIR 'JOG RGYU CHUNG ZAD KYANG MED PAS, DE'I SBRUL NI RTOG PAS BTAGS PA TZAM MO,
rows.wylie: 'grel pa der chags sogs rnams thag pa la sbrul du btags pa ltar gsungs pa ni mtshon pa tsam ste, chos gzhan thams cad kyang thag pa la sbrul du btags pa ltar rtog pas bzhag par 'chad pa'o, , de la khra bo'i mdog dang 'khyil lugs sbrul dang 'dra zhing , yul mi gsal bar snang ba na thag pa la 'di sbrul lo snyam pa 'byung ngo , , de'i tshe thag pa la thag pa'i tshogs pa dang cha shas sbrul gyi mtshan gzhir 'jog rgyu chung zad kyang med pas, de'i sbrul ni rtog pas btags pa tsam mo
rows.english: When this commentary states that "desire and such" are like a piece of rope labelled "snake," it is only giving a single example; what it means to say is that each and every other existing object is as well like a rope called a snake: they are all established through the process of conceptualization. Here the colored pattern of the rope and the way it's coiled make it resemble a snake; and if you're in a place where you can't see it very clearly, then you start to think to yourself, "It's a snake!" The fact though is that there is nothing about the rope as a whole, nor anything about its various parts, that you could ever establish as being one kind of a snake; the snake of the rope, then, is nothing but a creation of conceptions.

rows.english: The same thing happens when you get the idea of "me" about the heaps, the various components to yourself. There is nothing about these components as a whole, when you consider them as a continuum in time, nor as a whole considered in a single moment in time, nor as the various parts to a whole, that you could ever establish as being any kind of "me." We'll go into this in more detail further on.

rows.acip: `GNYIS PA RANG LUGS BZHAG PA LA, BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA CHU PHOR PA GANG LA, LAS CAN GYI LHA MI YI DVAGS GSUM GYIS CIG CAR DU BLTAS PA DE'I TSE, CHU PHOR PA GANG PO DE DNGOS PO GSUM GYI GZHI MTHUN PA MA YIN PA DANG , DE'I TSE TSAD MTSUNGS GSUM NGES PAR MI DGOS SHING , BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA CHU PHOR PA GANG PO DE CHA SHAS GSUM LDAN DU SKYE BA DANG ,
rows.wylie: `gnyis pa rang lugs bzhag pa la, brlan zhing gsher ba chu phor pa gang la, las can gyi lha mi yi dvags gsum gyis cig car du bltas pa de'i tshe, chu phor pa gang po de dngos po gsum gyi gzhi mthun pa ma yin pa dang , de'i tshe tshad mtshungs gsum nges par mi dgos shing , brlan zhing gsher ba chu phor pa gang po de cha shas gsum ldan du skye ba dang
rows.english: Here secondly is the section where we establish our own position. Now suppose three different types of beings--a pleasure being, a human, and a craving spirit, each with their own karma--sit down together and look upon a glass filled with water, the thing we define as "wet and flowing." The glass of water is not at this point one thing which is simultaneously three different objects. Neither is it necessary in this situation for there to be three identical valid perceptions. And when the glass full of wet and flowing water occurs, it occurs with three different, distinct parts to it.

rows.acip: DE YANG DANG POR GRUB TZAM NAS CHA SHAS GSUM LDAN DU GRUB CING , MTHAR MA ZHIG GI BAR DU CHA SHAS GSUM LDAN DU GNAS PA MA YIN TE, BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA CHU PHOR PA GANG PO DE'I CHA SHAS GCIG GIS NYER LEN DANG , YI DVAGS KYI LAS KYIS LHAN CIG BYED RKYEN BYAS PA LA BRTEN NAS DE'I CHA SHAS GCIG GI RIGS 'DRA PHYI MA RNAG KHRAG TU SKYE BA DANG ,
rows.wylie: de yang dang por grub tsam nas cha shas gsum ldan du grub cing , mthar ma zhig gi bar du cha shas gsum ldan du gnas pa ma yin te, brlan zhing gsher ba chu phor pa gang po de'i cha shas gcig gis nyer len dang , yi dvags kyi las kyis lhan cig byed rkyen byas pa la brten nas de'i cha shas gcig gi rigs 'dra phyi ma rnag khrag tu skye ba dang
rows.english: It is not though the case that, from the time it first started, the glass of water came with the three different parts, or that they stay with the glass of water until it eventually ends. What happens is that one of the parts of the glass filled with wet and flowing water provides a material cause, and the karma of the craving spirit provides a contributing factor; and then based on both of these the later continuation of one part of the glass of water starts being blood and pus.

rows.english: At this point, the glass full of wet and flowing water is something with three different parts. Nonetheless, it is not the case that all three different beings see all three parts. The craving spirit is forced by the bad karma he has collected to see the glass of water as pus and blood; and he doesn't see the other two things. One should understand that a similar case holds with the latter two types of beings.

rows.wylie: brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang la las can gyi 'gro ba gsum gyis cig car du bltas pa de'i tshe na dngos po tshad mas grub pa gsum skye ba'i dpe yang yod de, lcags gong dmar 'bar ba'i cha shas gcig gis nyer len dang lcags sngags kyis lhan cig byed rkyen byas pa la brten nas, lcags sngags btab pa'i lag pas reg pa de'i tshe na tsha ba'i reg bya mi myong reg bya gzhan zhig myong ba dang , lcags sngags ma btab pa'i lag pas reg pa de'i tshe na, tsha ba'i reg bya myong reg bya gzhan mi myong ba dang
rows.english: There is, moreover, an example we can use for how, when the three different types of beings with their three karmas look all together at a glass full of something wet and flowing, there start to be three different objects, each confirmed by a valid perception. Suppose there is a ball of red-hot steel; one piece of this ball provides the material cause, and the "mantra of steel" provides a contributing factor. Due to these two, a person who has used the mantra of steel on his hand can touch the ball, but he doesn't undergo any sensation of heat; instead, he feels some other sensation. A person who has not used the mantra on his hand touches the ball and does feel a sensation of heat, and no other kind of sensation.

rows.english: Another example would be the moon in springtime; one part of the feel of its rays on the body provides the material cause, and then the karma of a craving spirit provides a contributing factor. Based on these two, the spirit gets a sensation of heat, which is experienced by the consciousness of the body. So too with the wintertime sun; one part of the feel of its rays on the body provides the material cause, and then the karma of the craving spirit provides a contributing factor. Based on these two, the spirit gets a sensation of cold, which is experienced by the consciousness of the body.

rows.english: Here is the third part of our presentation, where we refute the rebuttal of representatives of other views. You will recall that our own position is describing a situation where beings of three different types, each with their own karma, are sitting together and looking at a glass filled with something that is wet and flowing. The glass filled with something wet and flowing exists, at this point, as something with three distinct parts. Nonetheless, no one of the beings is able to see all three things there, for they are each at the mercy of the particular karma that they themselves have collected. Representatives of other viewpoints now come to attack this position.

rows.wylie: chos thams cad rtog pas btags pa'i dpe ni, thag pa khra bo yul mi gsal ba na gnas pa'i tshe kha cig la 'di sbrul lo snyam pa'i blo 'byung ngo , , de'i tshe thag pa de'i tshogs pa dang cha shas gang yang sbrul du med kyang , de la sbrul lo snyam pa'i sbrul ni rtog pas btags pa tsam du 'char ro
rows.english: There is a metaphor used to describe how all existing things are labelled with our concepts. When you put a rope with a checkered pattern on it in a dark corner, some people might get the impression that it's a snake. The truth at this point though is that nothing about the rope is a snake: neither the rope as a whole, nor the parts of the rope. Nonetheless the person thinks of the rope as a snake, and this snake is an example of something which only makes its appearance as something labelled with a concept.

rows.acip: ,DE BZHIN DU PHUNG PO 'DI LA BRTEN NAS NGA'O SNYAM DU 'BYUNG YANG , PHUNG PO'I TSOGS PA DANG RGYUN DANG CHA SHAS GANG YANG NGA'I MTSAN GZHIR 'JOG RGYU MED CING , PHUNG PO LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA GZHAN ZHIG KYANG NGA'I MTSAN GZHIR BZUNG MED PAS, NGA DE NI PHUNG PO LA BRTEN NAS BTAGS PA TZAM YIN GYI, RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA MED DO,
rows.wylie: de bzhin du phung po 'di la brten nas nga'o snyam du 'byung yang , phung po'i tshogs pa dang rgyun dang cha shas gang yang nga'i mtshan gzhir 'jog rgyu med cing , phung po las ngo bo tha dad pa gzhan zhig kyang nga'i mtshan gzhir bzung med pas, nga de ni phung po la brten nas btags pa tsam yin gyi, rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa med do
rows.english: In the same way, the heaps of parts that make us up serve as a basis for us to get the impression "This is me." There is nothing at all about these heaps as a whole, nor their continuation over time, nor their separate components, that we could establish as being an actual representation of "me." At the same time though there is nothing else, nothing essentially separate from these heaps of parts to ourselves, that we could consider an actual representation of "me" either. As such, this "me" is merely something labelled upon the heaps of parts that make us up; there is nothing which exists by its own essence.

rows.english: This too is the point being made in the String of Precious Jewels, by the realized being Nagarjuna: If it's true that the persona is not the element Of earth, nor water, nor fire, nor wind, Not space, or consciousness, not all of them, Then how could he ever be anything else? The part of the verse that goes from "not earth" up to "not consciousness" is meant to deny that you could ever establish a self-nature of the person in any of the six elements that make up a persona, considered separately. The words "not all of them" are meant to deny that you could establish such a self-nature in the collection of the six elements, considered as a whole. The final line of the verse denies that there could be any self-nature which was essentially separate from these same elements.

rows.english: Just so none of these elements themselves exist purely, for they too are simply labelled upon the parts that they include. This same reasoning can be applied to the heaps of parts that make up a person, and all other objects as well: you can say about all of them that, because they are labelled on their parts and their whole, they do not exist independently. The physical heap of parts that I myself possess is something labelled upon my five appendages and so on; these appendages themselves are something labelled upon the body as a whole and the parts that go off to each side of it; and the smaller appendages like fingers and toes too are labelled upon their whole and their parts.

rows.english: A water pitcher is something labelled on its spout and base and other parts; the spout and base and such in turn are labelled on their parts and whole; and so on--the same pattern applies to all physical objects. Mental things too are labelled on mental events of successive moments, and through the objects towards which they function, and so on. Even uncaused phenomena are labelled upon the respective bases that take their labels. All this I have covered before, in other writings.

rows.acip: ,RGYU MTSAN NI, 'TSANG RGYA BA'I GNAS KYI ZHING GI BKOD PA PHUN SUM TSOGS PA RNAMS NI RGYU RKYEN DU MA TSOGS NAS BYUNG BA SGYU MA LTA BU'I BKOD PA YIN GYI, DON DAM PAR BKOD PA DE DAG MED PAR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR TE, 'ON KYANG MA BRTAG MA DPYAD PA'I BLO NGO NA YOD PAS THA SNYAD DU ZHING GI BKOD PA RNAMS ZHES BYA'O, , SANGS RGYAS KYI ZHING MA ZAD, SNOD BCUD KYI BKOD PA THAMS CAD KYANG CHA SHAS DU MA TSOGS PA LA BTAGS PA STE, KHANG PA LA SOGS PA BZHIN NO, , DE DAG THAMS CAD KYANG RIGS PAS RDUL PHRA RAB KYI BAR BSHIG NA CI YANG MA YIN PA'I BAR 'GYUR TE MTSON TZAM MO,
rows.wylie: rgyu mtshan ni, 'tshang rgya ba'i gnas kyi zhing gi bkod pa phun sum tshogs pa rnams ni rgyu rkyen du ma tshogs nas byung ba sgyu ma lta bu'i bkod pa yin gyi, don dam par bkod pa de dag med par de bzhin gshegs pas gsungs pa'i phyir te, 'on kyang ma brtag ma dpyad pa'i blo ngo na yod pas tha snyad du zhing gi bkod pa rnams zhes bya'o, , sangs rgyas kyi zhing ma zad, snod bcud kyi bkod pa thams cad kyang cha shas du ma tshogs pa la btags pa ste, khang pa la sogs pa bzhin no, , de dag thams cad kyang rigs pas rdul phra rab kyi bar bshig na ci yang ma yin pa'i bar 'gyur te mtshon tsam mo
rows.english: Why is this the case? The reason is that the Ones Thus Gone have stated that these perfect paradises, these places where you achieve your enlightenment, are put there like an illusion; that is, they occur because a great many causes and conditions have come together. But lands which have been put there in an ultimate sense, say the Buddhas, do not even exist. Since though they do exist to that state of mind which performs no check or analysis, we can nominally call them "paradise." This fact refers not only to the paradise of a Buddha, but also to each and every thing which has ever been put here: to both the world where beings live and the beings who live in the world. All of these are simply a label put on the collection of a number of parts: they are all the same as a house, for example. And all of these are such that, should you break them down mentally all the way to their tiniest atoms, you would reach the point where they are nothing at all. (This is the briefest sketch of the meaning for you.)

rows.acip: BDAG NI BRAN GYI NANG NAS KYANG KHUR LHAG PAR 'KHUR BA THA MA LTAR NGA RGYAL MED PAR SEMS CAN GYI DON RNAMS KUN LA BKOL BAR GYIS TE BDAG 'DI NI SKYON CAN GYI RANG BZHIN DU BSAM STE, THOS PA SOGS YON TAN CUNG ZAD KYI SGO NAS BSTOD PAR BYA'AM SNYAM NA, GLO BUR GYI YON TAN CHA SHAS TZAM GYIS KYANG MI BSTOD PAR BYANG SEMS GANG LA DMIGS NAS 'DI'I YON TAN CI NAS KYANG GANG ZAG 'AGS KYANG MI SHES PA DE LTAR GSANG BAR GYIS SHIG PA STE, RANG GI YON TAN MI SGROG PAR BSAM PA'O,
rows.wylie: bdag ni bran gyi nang nas kyang khur lhag par 'khur ba tha ma ltar nga rgyal med par sems can gyi don rnams kun la bkol bar gyis te bdag 'di ni skyon can gyi rang bzhin du bsam ste, thos pa sogs yon tan cung zad kyi sgo nas bstod par bya'am snyam na, glo bur gyi yon tan cha shas tsam gyis kyang mi bstod par byang sems gang la dmigs nas 'di'i yon tan ci nas kyang gang zag 'ags kyang mi shes pa de ltar gsang bar gyis shig pa ste, rang gi yon tan mi sgrog par bsam pa'o
rows.english: Let me command myself to work for every purpose needed by other living beings, acting as if I were the least of servants, accepting every extra load, without any kind of pride as I do so. Let me reflect upon how he, meaning me, is by his very nature wrong. And if it occurs to me that I should praise him for some minute good quality that he might have, something like a little learning, then let me think the following. I will refuse to praise him for some small and insignificant good qualities he may acquire by accident; I will see to it that any qualities which he, this bodhisattva, does have are not detected by anyone else at all. And thus it is that we must be sure to keep our good qualities secret, and contemplate upon the practice of never publicizing them at all. Contemplation Thirty-Nine The endless thirst of attachment to your own needs

rows.english: Therefore it would be wrong to consider, even nominally, either the whole of the parts of a person, or the stream of the mind, or any of the components or parts of a person to be the thing we refer to as the "person." Neither is there anything that can we decide is the person and which is essentially different from these things. Therefore the simple fact of the matter is that the person is something which is merely imposed upon all these.

rows.wylie: 'o na khyod rang gi lugs ji ltar yin zhe na phung po'i rgyun gcig la ni brten su las byed pa po dang 'bras bu spyod pa po zhes bya bar bstan pa ste bdags so, , rgyun zhes pa ni cha shas su gyur pa'i skad cig snga phyi bar gsum nye bar blang byar yod pa'i cha can nye bar len pa po ste mdor na gang zag 'dis las kyang byas 'bras bu yang myong zhes pa 'thad kyi rgyu 'bras dus gcig pa sus kyang bzhag mi nus so
rows.english: "Well then," you may continue, "what is your own position in this regard?" We can point to someone as--that is, name someone as--"the one who performs the karma" and "the one who experiences the result" all with reference to a single continuous stream of the parts or heaps to a person. The term "continuous stream" here refers to a whole, the person to whom the various parts belong; and these parts are the moments of them that exist earlier, later, and in between, and which belong to the person. To summarize, it is entirely correct to say that any one person has both committed a karma and experienced its consequences; it's not the case though that cause and effect are then simultaneous--no one could ever show that was the case.

rows.acip: DPER NA CHU SHING GI SDONG PO DAG CHA SHAS SU PHYE NA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA 'GA' YANG MED PA DE BZHIN DU RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB MA GRUB RIGS PAS RNAM PAR DPYAD PA YIS BTZAL NA BDAG KYANG YANG DAG PAR GRUB PA MIN TE 'OG NAS 'CHAD PA'I BDAG MED SGRUB PA'I RIGS PAS GNOD PA'I PHYIR RO,
rows.wylie: dper na chu shing gi sdong po dag cha shas su phye na rang bzhin gyis grub pa 'ga' yang med pa de bzhin du rang bzhin gyis grub ma grub rigs pas rnam par dpyad pa yis btsal na bdag kyang yang dag par grub pa min te 'og nas 'chad pa'i bdag med sgrub pa'i rigs pas gnod pa'i phyir ro
rows.english: Think for example of a hollow reed: when you strip away the stem piece by piece, you find in the end that there is nothing with any nature at all. Here it's exactly the same: you use logic to try to find out whether things have any nature of their own or not, and come to the conclusion that there is no "myself" that you could ever correctly decide existed. The idea that such a self could exist is disproved totally by the various reasonings used, as I will describe below, to establish that nothing has any self-nature at all. rows.english: The hand too then is just The same; a collection of fingers, So how could it ever be? rows.english: And even these atoms can be divided then into their own parts: into their eastern side, and so on. They too then are a concept applied to the collection of the multiple sides that face in the different directions, and so they have no nature of their own either. Things then are devoid of any parts that have any nature of their own; and so they are just like, for example, empty space.

rows.wylie: `gnyis pa rang lugs bzhag pa la, brlan zhing gsher ba chu phor pa gang la, las can gyi lha mi yi dvags gsum gyis cig car du bltas pa de'i tshe, chu phor pa gang po de dngos po gsum gyi gzhi mthun pa ma yin pa dang , de'i tshe tshad mtshungs gsum nges par mi dgos shing , brlan zhing gsher ba chu phor pa gang po de cha shas gsum ldan du skye ba dang
rows.english: Here secondly is the section where we establish our own position. Now suppose three different types of beings--a pleasure being, a human, and a craving spirit, each with their own karma--sit down together and look upon a glass filled with water, the thing we define as "wet and flowing." The glass of water is not at this point one thing which is simultaneously three different objects. Neither is it necessary in this situation for there to be three identical valid perceptions. And when the glass full of wet and flowing water occurs, it occurs with three different, distinct parts to it. [Translator's note: When the phrase "wet and flowing" (the definition of the element of water) is used here, it should be understood as emphasizing the more general concept of a liquid, rather than the water which the human perceives.]

rows.acip: DE YANG DANG POR GRUB TZAM NAS CHA SHAS GSUM LDAN DU GRUB CING , MTHAR MA ZHIG GI BAR DU CHA SHAS GSUM LDAN DU GNAS PA MA YIN TE, BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA CHU PHOR PA GANG PO DE'I CHA SHAS GCIG GIS NYER LEN DANG , YI DVAGS KYI LAS KYIS LHAN CIG BYED RKYEN BYAS PA LA BRTEN NAS DE'I CHA SHAS GCIG GI RIGS 'DRA PHYI MA RNAG KHRAG TU SKYE BA DANG ,
rows.wylie: de yang dang por grub tsam nas cha shas gsum ldan du grub cing , mthar ma zhig gi bar du cha shas gsum ldan du gnas pa ma yin te, brlan zhing gsher ba chu phor pa gang po de'i cha shas gcig gis nyer len dang , yi dvags kyi las kyis lhan cig byed rkyen byas pa la brten nas de'i cha shas gcig gi rigs 'dra phyi ma rnag khrag tu skye ba dang
rows.english: It is not though the case that, from the time it first started, the glass of water came with the three different parts, or that they stay with the glass of water until it eventually ends. What happens is that one of the parts of the glass filled with wet and flowing water provides a material cause, and the karma of the craving spirit provides a contributing factor; and then based on both of these the later continuation of one part of the glass of water starts being blood and pus.

One should understand that a similar case holds with the latter two types of beings.

rows.english: There is, moreover, an example we can use for how, when the three different types of beings with their three karmas look all together at a glass full of something wet and flowing, there start to be three different objects, each confirmed by a valid perception. Suppose there is a ball of red-hot steel; one piece of this ball provides the material cause, and the "mantra of steel" provides a contributing factor. Due to these two, a person who has used the mantra of steel on his hand can touch the ball, but he doesn't undergo any sensation of heat; instead, he feels some other sensation. A person who has not used the mantra on his hand touches the ball and does feel a sensation of heat, and no other kind of sensation.

rows.english: Another example would be the moon in springtime; one part of the feel of its rays on the body provides the material cause, and then the karma of a craving spirit provides a contributing factor. Based on these two, the spirit gets a sensation cold, which is experienced by the consciousness of the body.

rows.english: Here is the third part of our presentation, where we refute the rebuttal of representatives of other views. You will recall that our own position is describing a situation where beings of three different types, each with their own karma, are sitting together and looking at a glass filled with something that is wet and flowing. The glass filled with something wet and flowing exists, at this point, as something with three distinct parts. Nonetheless, no one of the beings is able to see all three things there, for they are each at the mercy of the particular karma that they themselves have collected. Representatives of other viewpoints now come to attack this position.

rows.acip: ,'GREL PA DER CHAGS SOGS RNAMS THAG PA LA SBRUL DU BTAGS PA LTAR GSUNGS PA NI MTSON PA TZAM STE, CHOS GZHAN THAMS CAD KYANG THAG PA LA SBRUL DU BTAGS PA LTAR RTOG PAS BZHAG PAR 'CHAD PA'O, , DE LA KHRA BO'I MDOG DANG 'KHYIL LUGS SBRUL DANG 'DRA ZHING , YUL MI GSAL BAR SNANG BA NA THAG PA LA 'DI SBRUL LO SNYAM PA 'BYUNG NGO , , DE'I TSE THAG PA LA THAG PA'I TSOGS PA DANG CHA SHAS SBRUL GYI MTSAN GZHIR 'JOG RGYU CHUNG ZAD KYANG MED PAS, DE'I SBRUL NI RTOG PAS BTAGS PA TZAM MO,
rows.wylie: 'grel pa der chags sogs rnams thag pa la sbrul du btags pa ltar gsungs pa ni mtshon pa tsam ste, chos gzhan thams cad kyang thag pa la sbrul du btags pa ltar rtog pas bzhag par 'chad pa'o, , de la khra bo'i mdog dang 'khyil lugs sbrul dang 'dra zhing , yul mi gsal bar snang ba na thag pa la 'di sbrul lo snyam pa 'byung ngo , , de'i tshe thag pa la thag pa'i tshogs pa dang cha shas sbrul gyi mtshan gzhir 'jog rgyu chung zad kyang med pas, de'i sbrul ni rtog pas btags pa tsam mo
rows.english: When this commentary states that "desire and such" are like a piece of rope labelled "snake," it is only giving a single example; what it means to say is that each and every other existing object is as well like a rope called a snake: they are all established through the process of projection. Here the colored pattern of the rope and the way it's coiled make it resemble a snake; and if you're in a place where you can't see it very clearly, then you start to think to yourself, "It's a snake!" The fact though is that there is nothing about the rope as a whole, nor anything about its various parts, that you could ever establish as being one kind of a snake; the snake of the rope, then, is nothing but a creation of projections.

rows.english: Here secondly is the section where we establish our own position. Now suppose three different types of beings--a pleasure being, a human, and a craving spirit, each with their own karma--sit down together and look upon a glass filled with water, the thing we define as "wet and flowing." The glass of water is not at this point one thing which is simultaneously three different objects. Neither is it necessary in this situation for there to be three identical valid perceptions. And when the glass full of wet and flowing water occurs, it occurs with three different, distinct parts to it.

And when the glass full of wet and flowing water occurs, it occurs with three different, distinct parts to it."}

rows.acip: DE YANG DANG POR GRUB TZAM NAS CHA SHAS GSUM LDAN DU GRUB CING , MTHAR MA ZHIG GI BAR DU CHA SHAS GSUM LDAN DU GNAS PA MA YIN TE, BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA CHU PHOR PA GANG PO DE'I CHA SHAS GCIG GIS NYER LEN DANG , YI DVAGS KYI LAS KYIS LHAN CIG BYED RKYEN BYAS PA LA BRTEN NAS DE'I CHA SHAS GCIG GI RIGS 'DRA PHYI MA RNAG KHRAG TU SKYE BA DANG ,
rows.wylie: de yang dang por grub tsam nas cha shas gsum ldan du grub cing , mthar ma zhig gi bar du cha shas gsum ldan du gnas pa ma yin te, brlan zhing gsher ba chu phor pa gang po de'i cha shas gcig gis nyer len dang , yi dvags kyi las kyis lhan cig byed rkyen byas pa la brten nas de'i cha shas gcig gi rigs 'dra phyi ma rnag khrag tu skye ba dang
rows.english: It is not though the case that, from the time it first started, the glass of water came with the three different parts, or that they stay with the glass of water until it eventually ends. What happens is that one of the parts of the glass filled with wet and flowing water provides a material cause, and the karma of the craving spirit provides a contributing factor; and then based on both of these the later continuation of one part of the glass of water starts being blood and pus.

rows.wylie: de'i tshe na brlan zhing gsher ba chu phor pa gang po de cha shas gsum ldan du yod kyang , gsum gas gsum ga mthong ba ma yin te, yi dvags kyi las ngan pa bsags pa'i dbang gis rnag khrag tu mthong , dngos po gzhan gnyis ma mthong ba dang , de bzhin du 'gro ba 'og ma gnyis la yang shes par bya ba yin pa'i phyir
rows.english: At this point, the glass full of wet and flowing water is something with three different parts. Nonetheless, it is not the case that all three different beings see all three parts. The craving spirit is forced by the bad karma he has collected to see the glass of water as pus and blood; and he doesn't see the other two things. One should understand that a similar case holds with the latter two types of beings.

rows.wylie: chos thams cad rtog pas btags pa'i dpe ni, thag pa khra bo yul mi gsal ba na gnas pa'i tshe kha cig la 'di sbrul lo snyam pa'i blo 'byung ngo , , de'i tshe thag pa de'i tshogs pa dang cha shas gang yang sbrul du med kyang , de la sbrul lo snyam pa'i sbrul ni rtog pas btags pa tsam du 'char ro
rows.english: There is a metaphor used to describe how all existing things are labelled with our concepts. When you put a rope with a checkered pattern on it in a dark corner, some people might get the impression that it's a snake. The truth at this point though is that nothing about the rope is a snake: neither the rope as a whole, nor the parts of the rope. Nonetheless the person thinks of the rope as a snake, and this snake is an example of something which only makes its appearance as something labelled with a concept.

rows.acip: ,DE BZHIN DU PHUNG PO 'DI LA BRTEN NAS NGA'O SNYAM DU 'BYUNG YANG , PHUNG PO'I TSOGS PA DANG RGYUN DANG CHA SHAS GANG YANG NGA'I MTSAN GZHIR 'JOG RGYU MED CING , PHUNG PO LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA GZHAN ZHIG KYANG NGA'I MTSAN GZHIR BZUNG MED PAS, NGA DE NI PHUNG PO LA BRTEN NAS BTAGS PA TZAM YIN GYI, RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA MED DO,
rows.wylie: de bzhin du phung po 'di la brten nas nga'o snyam du 'byung yang , phung po'i tshogs pa dang rgyun dang cha shas gang yang nga'i mtshan gzhir 'jog rgyu med cing , phung po las ngo bo tha dad pa gzhan zhig kyang nga'i mtshan gzhir bzung med pas, nga de ni phung po la brten nas btags pa tsam yin gyi, rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa med do
rows.english: In the same way, the heaps of parts that make us up serve as a basis for us to get the impression "This is me." There is nothing at all about these heaps as a whole, nor their continuation over time, nor their separate components, that we could establish as being an actual representation of "me." At the same time though there is nothing else, nothing essentially separate from these heaps of parts to ourselves, that we could consider an actual representation of "me" either. As such, this "me" is merely something labelled upon the heaps of parts that make us up; there is nothing which exists by its own essence. ************

rows.acip: ,RGYU MTSAN NI, 'TSANG RGYA BA'I GNAS KYI ZHING GI BKOD PA PHUN SUM TSOGS PA RNAMS NI RGYU RKYEN DU MA TSOGS NAS BYUNG BA SGYU MA LTA BU'I BKOD PA YIN GYI, DON DAM PAR BKOD PA DE DAG MED PAR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PAS GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR TE, 'ON KYANG MA BRTAG MA DPYAD PA'I BLO NGO NA YOD PAS THA SNYAD DU ZHING GI BKOD PA RNAMS ZHES BYA'O, , SANGS RGYAS KYI ZHING MA ZAD, SNOD BCUD KYI BKOD PA THAMS CAD KYANG CHA SHAS DU MA TSOGS PA LA BTAGS PA STE, KHANG PA LA SOGS PA BZHIN NO, , DE DAG THAMS CAD KYANG RIGS PAS RDUL PHRA RAB KYI BAR BSHIG NA CI YANG MA YIN PA'I BAR 'GYUR TE MTSON TZAM MO,
rows.wylie: rgyu mtshan ni, 'tshang rgya ba'i gnas kyi zhing gi bkod pa phun sum tshogs pa rnams ni rgyu rkyen du ma tshogs nas byung ba sgyu ma lta bu'i bkod pa yin gyi, don dam par bkod pa de dag med par de bzhin gshegs pas gsungs pa'i phyir te, 'on kyang ma brtag ma dpyad pa'i blo ngo na yod pas tha snyad du zhing gi bkod pa rnams zhes bya'o, , sangs rgyas kyi zhing ma zad, snod bcud kyi bkod pa thams cad kyang cha shas du ma tshogs pa la btags pa ste, khang pa la sogs pa bzhin no, , de dag thams cad kyang rigs pas rdul phra rab kyi bar bshig na ci yang ma yin pa'i bar 'gyur te mtshon tsam mo
rows.english: Why is this the case? The reason is that the Ones Thus Gone have stated that these perfect paradises, these places where you achieve your enlightenment, are put there like an illusion; that is, they occur because a great many causes and conditions have come together. But lands which have been put there in an ultimate sense, say the Buddhas, do not even exist. Since though they do exist to that state of mind which performs no check or analysis, we can nominally call them "paradise." This fact refers not only to the paradise of a Buddha, but also to each and every thing which has ever been put here: to both the world where beings live and the beings who live in the world. All of these are simply a label put on the collection of a number of parts: they are all the same as a house, for example. And all of these are such that, should you break them down mentally all the way to their tiniest atoms, you would reach the point where they are nothing at all. (This is the briefest sketch of the meaning for you.) ************ 17 The Emptiness of Every Object

rows.acip: ,DES NA THA SNYAD DU YANG PHUNG PO'I TSOGS PA DANG RGYUN DANG YA GYAL DANG CHA SHAS GANG YANG GANG ZAG GI MTSAN GZHIR GZUNG DU MI RUNG LA, DE RNAMS LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA GZHAN YANG GANG ZAG TU BZHAG TU MED DE DE DAG LA BRTEN NAS GANG ZAG TU BTAGS PA TZAM DU ZAD PA'O,
rows.wylie: des na tha snyad du yang phung po'i tshogs pa dang rgyun dang ya gyal dang cha shas gang yang gang zag gi mtshan gzhir gzung du mi rung la, de rnams las ngo bo tha dad pa gzhan yang gang zag tu bzhag tu med de de dag la brten nas gang zag tu btags pa tsam du zad pa'o
rows.english: Therefore it would be wrong to consider, even nominally, either the whole of the parts of a person, or the stream of the mind, or any of the components or parts of a person to be the thing we refer to as the "person." Neither is there anything that can we decide is the person and which is essentially different from these things. Therefore the simple fact of the matter is that the person is something which is merely imposed upon all these.

rows.acip: ,'O NA KHYOD RANG GI LUGS JI LTAR YIN ZHE NA PHUNG PO'I RGYUN GCIG LA NI BRTEN SU LAS BYED PA PO DANG 'BRAS BU SPYOD PA PO ZHES BYA BAR BSTAN PA STE BDAGS SO, , RGYUN ZHES PA NI CHA SHAS SU GYUR PA'I SKAD CIG SNGA PHYI BAR GSUM NYE BAR BLANG BYAR YOD PA'I CHA CAN NYE BAR LEN PA PO STE MDOR NA GANG ZAG 'DIS LAS KYANG BYAS 'BRAS BU YANG MYONG ZHES PA 'THAD KYI RGYU 'BRAS DUS GCIG PA SUS KYANG BZHAG MI NUS SO,
rows.wylie: 'o na khyod rang gi lugs ji ltar yin zhe na phung po'i rgyun gcig la ni brten su las byed pa po dang 'bras bu spyod pa po zhes bya bar bstan pa ste bdags so, , rgyun zhes pa ni cha shas su gyur pa'i skad cig snga phyi bar gsum nye bar blang byar yod pa'i cha can nye bar len pa po ste mdor na gang zag 'dis las kyang byas 'bras bu yang myong zhes pa 'thad kyi rgyu 'bras dus gcig pa sus kyang bzhag mi nus so
rows.english: "Well then," you may continue, "what is your own position in this regard?" We can point to someone as--that is, name someone as--"the one who performs the karma" and "the one who experiences the result" all with reference to a single continuous stream of the parts or heaps to a person. The term "continuous stream" here refers to a whole, the person to whom the various parts belong; and these parts are the moments of them that exist earlier, later, and in between, and which belong to the person. To summarize, it is entirely correct to say that any one person has both committed a karma and experienced its consequences; it's not the case though that cause and effect are then simultaneous--no one could ever show that was the case.

rows.acip: DPER NA CHU SHING GI SDONG PO DAG CHA SHAS SU PHYE NA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA 'GA' YANG MED PA DE BZHIN DU RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB MA GRUB RIGS PAS RNAM PAR DPYAD PA YIS BTZAL NA BDAG KYANG YANG DAG PAR GRUB PA MIN TE 'OG NAS 'CHAD PA'I BDAG MED SGRUB PA'I RIGS PAS GNOD PA'I PHYIR RO,
rows.wylie: dper na chu shing gi sdong po dag cha shas su phye na rang bzhin gyis grub pa 'ga' yang med pa de bzhin du rang bzhin gyis grub ma grub rigs pas rnam par dpyad pa yis btsal na bdag kyang yang dag par grub pa min te 'og nas 'chad pa'i bdag med sgrub pa'i rigs pas gnod pa'i phyir ro
rows.english: Think for example of a hollow reed: when you strip away the stem piece by piece, you find in the end that there is nothing with any nature at all. Here it's exactly the same: you use logic to try to find out whether things have any nature of their own or not, and come to the conclusion that there is no "myself" that you could ever correctly decide existed. The idea that such a self could exist is disproved totally by the various reasonings used, as I will describe below, to establish that nothing has any self-nature at all. 130 The Asian Classics Institute Course XVIII: The Great Ideas of Buddhism, Part Three Reading Four: The Guide to the Bodhisattva's Way of Life, Sixth of Six Parts The following contemplations are based on the Guide to the Bodhisattva's Way of Life (Bodhisattvacharyavatara; Byang-chub-sems-dpa'i spyod-pa la 'jug-pa) of the Buddhist master Shantideva (circa 700 AD), and the commentary upon it by Gyaltsab Je Darma Rinchen (1364-1432) entitled Entry Point for Children of the Victorious Buddhas (rGyal-sras 'jug-ngogs). The relevant sections are found at folios 33B-34A and 137B-140B, respectively, in the ACIP electronic editions TD3871 and S5436. The content of the contemplations is translated directly from the root text and commentary; the names of the contemplations are not a part of the original text, but are based on the divisions of Gyaltsab Je's commentary and have been supplied for reference. ************ Further Contemplations on the Perfection of Wisdo

rows.english: The hand too then is just The same; a collection of fingers, So how could it ever be? Each in turn is a collection Of joints; and if you divide The joints into parts, and then Divide the parts down to atoms, And then divide these into Sides in different directions, Then things are devoid of parts, And just like empty space; So even the atoms have none.

rows.english: And even these atoms can be divided then into their own parts: into their eastern side, and so on. Things then are devoid of any parts that have any nature of their own; and so they are just like, for example, empty space.

rows.acip: `GNYIS PA RANG LUGS BZHAG PA LA, BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA CHU PHOR PA GANG LA, LAS CAN GYI LHA MI YI DVAGS GSUM GYIS CIG CAR DU BLTAS PA DE'I TSE, CHU PHOR PA GANG PO DE DNGOS PO GSUM GYI GZHI MTHUN PA MA YIN PA DANG , DE'I TSE TSAD MTSUNGS GSUM NGES PAR MI DGOS SHING , BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA CHU PHOR PA GANG PO DE CHA SHAS GSUM LDAN DU SKYE BA DANG ,
rows.wylie: `gnyis pa rang lugs bzhag pa la, brlan zhing gsher ba chu phor pa gang la, las can gyi lha mi yi dvags gsum gyis cig car du bltas pa de'i tshe, chu phor pa gang po de dngos po gsum gyi gzhi mthun pa ma yin pa dang , de'i tshe tshad mtshungs gsum nges par mi dgos shing , brlan zhing gsher ba chu phor pa gang po de cha shas gsum ldan du skye ba dang
rows.english: Here secondly is the section where we establish our own position. Now suppose three different types of beings--a pleasure being, a human, and a craving spirit, each with their own karma--sit down together and look upon a glass filled with water, the thing we define as "wet and flowing." The glass of water is not at this point one thing which is simultaneously three different objects. Neither is it necessary in this situation for there to be three identical valid perceptions. And when the glass full of wet and flowing water occurs, it occurs with three different, distinct parts to it. [Translator's note: When the phrase "wet and flowing" (the definition of the element of water) is used here, it should be understood as emphasizing the more general concept of a liquid, rather than the water which the human perceives.]

rows.acip: DE YANG DANG POR GRUB TZAM NAS CHA SHAS GSUM LDAN DU GRUB CING , MTHAR MA ZHIG GI BAR DU CHA SHAS GSUM LDAN DU GNAS PA MA YIN TE, BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA CHU PHOR PA GANG PO DE'I CHA SHAS GCIG GIS NYER LEN DANG , YI DVAGS KYI LAS KYIS LHAN CIG BYED RKYEN BYAS PA LA BRTEN NAS DE'I CHA SHAS GCIG GI RIGS 'DRA PHYI MA RNAG KHRAG TU SKYE BA DANG ,
rows.wylie: de yang dang por grub tsam nas cha shas gsum ldan du grub cing , mthar ma zhig gi bar du cha shas gsum ldan du gnas pa ma yin te, brlan zhing gsher ba chu phor pa gang po de'i cha shas gcig gis nyer len dang , yi dvags kyi las kyis lhan cig byed rkyen byas pa la brten nas de'i cha shas gcig gi rigs 'dra phyi ma rnag khrag tu skye ba dang
rows.english: It is not though the case that, from the time it first started, the glass of water came with the three different parts, or that they stay with the glass of water until it eventually ends. What happens is that one of the parts of the glass filled with wet and flowing water provides a material cause, and the karma of the craving spirit provides a contributing factor; and then based on both of these the later continuation of one part of the glass of water starts being blood and pus.

One should understand that a similar case holds with the latter two types of beings.

rows.english: There is, moreover, an example we can use for how, when the three different types of beings with their three karmas look all together at a glass full of something wet and flowing, there start to be three different objects, each confirmed by a valid perception. Suppose there is a ball of red-hot steel; one piece of this ball provides the material cause, and the "mantra of steel" provides a contributing factor. Due to these two, a person who has used the mantra of steel on his hand can touch the ball, but he doesn't undergo any sensation of heat; instead, he feels some other sensation. A person who has not used the mantra on his hand touches the ball and does feel a sensation of heat, and no other kind of sensation.

rows.english: Another example would be the moon in springtime; one part of the feel of its rays on the body provides the material cause, and then the karma of a craving spirit provides a contributing factor. Based on these two, the spirit gets a sensation cold, which is experienced by the consciousness of the body.

rows.wylie: rgyas par zung du bsgrubs yod aang, ,cha shas tshogs pa'ang khyod min zhing, ,re re'ang khyod min khyod kyang min
rows.english: You could go further and check Whether it goes both ways: The sum of all your parts is not you, Nor is it that any one part is you; And neither can we say That you are you! The grand, unifying picture of you is not you by itself either, without all the component pictures that it ties together.  Truly feeling that I am an individual—like everything else in the universe—depends on the appropriate picture for that feeling.  What would be the karmic cause—how would we have to treat others around us—to see this picture coming out of our mind, as the karmic seed opens? Mental parts & wholes

rows.acip: ,NGA PHUNG BDEN PA'I GCIG GRUB NA, ,PHUNG PO'I CHA SHAS KUN DANG NI, ,BDEN PA'I GCIG TU GRUB DGOS PAS, ,SHAR NUB LHO BYANG DBUS DBYE BA'I, ,PHYOGS NI GANG DU GCIG PAR 'GYUR,
rows.wylie: nga phung bden pa'i gcig grub na, ,phung po'i cha shas kun dang ni, ,bden pa'i gcig tu grub dgos pas, ,shar nub lho byang dbus dbye ba'i, ,phyogs ni gang du gcig par 'gyur
rows.english: If the “me” were, In reality, One with my body & mind, Then the “me” would have to be, In reality, One with each and every one Of the separate parts of body & mind. And then the “me” would be One with each of the separate Directions of east, and west, South, and north, and middle. If I am—from my own side—equivalent to the sum of the parts of my body and mind, then I should equally be equivalent to the sum of each of their parts: hands and feet, sadness and happiness. The physical parts of me have further divisions into those to the left, and those to the right; or, we can say, corresponding for example to north and south.  A whole which existed from its own side would also have to include the extent of all the parts of each of the directions—and thus be as large as the universe itself.

rows.english: I disagree that if something were one thing which existed in truth, then it would have to be a singular object without any parts of its own. And yet it would have to be, Because if a thing were divided into parts, then these parts would exist through relying on each other; and it would then be a contradiction to say that the thing existed in truth.

rows.acip: DE BZHIN DU RANG GI PHUNG PO'I STENG DU NGA'O SNYAM PA'I BLO SKYE BA NA PHUNG PO'I TSOGS RGYUN DANG CHA SHAS DANG DBYIBS SOGS GANG YANG NGAR 'JOG TU MI RUNG YANG, RTOG PAS BTAGS PA'I NGA TZAM ZHIG NI THA SNYAD DU YOD DO,,
rows.wylie: de bzhin du rang gi phung po'i steng du nga'o snyam pa'i blo skye ba na phung po'i tshogs rgyun dang cha shas dang dbyibs sogs gang yang ngar 'jog tu mi rung yang, rtog pas btags pa'i nga tsam zhig ni tha snyad du yod do
rows.english: The same thing happens when the thought comes up in our mind—as it focuses on our body and mind—that “This is me!” There is nothing in the collection of our body and mind—not in the moment, nor over a period of time; nor in the separate parts, nor in the shapes and so on—which we can point to as being “me.” And yet there does exist there, nominally speaking, a simple “me” which is projected by our conceptions.

rows.acip: DER THAL, CHOS THAMS CAD GDAGS GZHI CHA SHAS GZHAN LA BRTEN NAS BZHAG PA'I RTEN 'BYUNG YIN PA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: der thal, chos thams cad gdags gzhi cha shas gzhan la brten nas bzhag pa'i rten 'byung yin pa'i phyir
rows.english: And that is so the case, because each and every object in the universe displays a kind of interdependence, where it is established as existing dependent upon something that receives its name: parts which are something other than that object itself.

rows.acip: DANG PO NI, CHOS THAMS CAD KYANG, RANG GI CHA SHAS DANG, CHA SHAS RNAMS KYANG RANG RANG GI CHA SHAS DANG BCAS PA YIN TSUL GONG GI CHA MED 'GOG PA'I RIGS PAS SHES DGOS LA,
rows.wylie: dang po ni, chos thams cad kyang, rang gi cha shas dang, cha shas rnams kyang rang rang gi cha shas dang bcas pa yin tshul gong gi cha med 'gog pa'i rigs pas shes dgos la
rows.english: The first of these you should learn from our earlier presentation, where we explained the logic behind denying that there exists anything which doesn't have its own parts. This is based on the way in which things come with their own parts, and then those parts in turn come each with their own parts.

rows.acip: MDOR NA, RANG GI CHA SHAS DANG SGRA RTOG GIS BZHAG PA LA MA BLTOS PAR RANG DBANG DU GRUB PA'I CHOS MED PAS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I CHOS MED PA YIN TE,
rows.wylie: mdor na, rang gi cha shas dang sgra rtog gis bzhag pa la ma bltos par rang dbang du grub pa'i chos med pas rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i chos med pa yin te
rows.english: We can, in short, say that there is no object in the universe which exists through any nature of its own—which exists in and of itself, without depending on a process where its existence is established through the application of words and mental pictures to its assembled parts.

rows.acip: SHES BYA'AM DNGOS PO LA DBYE NA, BDEN PA GNYIS SU YOD, BCOM PA'AM BLOS CHA SHAS SO SOR GSAL BA NA RANG 'DZIN GYI BLO 'DOR DU RUNG BA'I CHOS RNAMS NI KUN RDZOB BDEN PA YIN LA,
rows.wylie: shes bya'am dngos po la dbye na, bden pa gnyis su yod, bcom pa'am blos cha shas so sor gsal ba na rang 'dzin gyi blo 'dor du rung ba'i chos rnams ni kun rdzob bden pa yin la
rows.english: They assert that all knowable things—which then is to say, all functioning things—can be divided into two different realities.  The first one, deceptive reality, they describe as consisting of all of those objects which exist in a way such that—when they are destroyed, or broken down by the mind into their various constituent parts—then the state of mind which holds them must also fade away.

The first one, deceptive reality, they describe as consisting of all of those objects which exist in a way such that—when they are destroyed, or broken down by the mind into their various constituent parts—then the state of mind which holds them must also fade away."}

rows.acip: BCOM PA'AM BLOS CHA SHAS SO SOR BSAL BA NA RANG 'DZIN GYI BLO MI 'DOR BA'I CHOS RNAMS DON DAM BDEN PA YIN LA, BSAM DON NI SNGAR GYI ZLOG PHYOGS KYIS SHES SHING,

rows.english: Consider, on the other hand, any object which exists in such a way that—when it is destroyed, or broken down by the mind into its various constituent parts—the state of mind which holds to it does not fade away.  Things like this they call “ultimate reality”; and the idea here we can grasp by thinking of the opposite of what was said before.

rows.english: Let's consider the collection of six different types of consciousness. Are you saying that they extend to each and every one of the sections of the body? Why do you say that? Because they do constitute the state of awareness which accomplishes taking on a body during rebirth.

rows.acip: [E13] BZHI PA GRUB STE, DBANG SHES RNAMS LUS KYI PHYOGS LA BRTEN PA GANG ZHIG ,YID SHES NI LUS KYI CHA SHAS LA MI GNAS KYANG LUS THAMS CAD LA KHYAB NAS 'DZIN PA'I NUS PA MED PA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: [e13] bzhi pa grub ste, dbang shes rnams lus kyi phyogs la brten pa gang zhig ,yid shes ni lus kyi cha shas la mi gnas kyang lus thams cad la khyab nas 'dzin pa'i nus pa med pa'i phyir
rows.english: The fourth reason is correct because the sense consciousnesses are something that depend upon different areas of the physical body; whereas the consciousness of the thought—although it is not situated at any one part of the body—still lacks the capacity to grasp its object even as it extends over the entire body.

rows.acip: DE'I TSE THAG PA LA THAG PA'I TSOGS PA DANG CHA SHAS SBRUL GYI MTSAN GZHIR 'JOG RGYU CUNG ZAD KYANG MED PAS, DE'I SBRUL NI RTOG PAS BTAGS PA TZAM MO,,

rows.english: The word “individual” here refers to the person; or the living being; the “I” or the “self.” The list of what it is not—which goes from “earth” up to “consciousness”—refers to the parts of a living being: the six elements which make them up. The phrase “none of these” is meant to deny that there is any combination of these elements which we can posit as being the person. And then the final part serves to deny that there is something which is such that to be it would not to be the person, which could still be posited as being the person.

rows.acip: LUGS DANG PO LA NI, MYU GU LTA BU'I DNGOS PO CIG ZHIG PA NA, MYU GU'I CHA SHAS KYI DNGOS PO THAMS CAD NI LOG LA, MYU GU LAS GZHAN PA BUM PA LA SOGS PA'I DNGOS PO GZHAN GANG YANG MA THOB PAS, ZHIG PA DE DNGOS PO GTAN MIN PAR 'DOD DE, SNGON PO LA SOGS PA SKYE MCHED RE RE BA'I DNGOS PO DANG, BUM PA LA SOGS PA RANG GI CHA SHAS KYI DNGOS PO TSOGS PA GANG YANG ZHIG PA DE'I MTSAN GZHIR MI RUNG BA'I PHYIR DNGOS PO MIN NO SNYAM PA'O,,
rows.wylie: lugs dang po la ni, myu gu lta bu'i dngos po cig zhig pa na, myu gu'i cha shas kyi dngos po thams cad ni log la, myu gu las gzhan pa bum pa la sogs pa'i dngos po gzhan gang yang ma thob pas, zhig pa de dngos po gtan min par 'dod de, sngon po la sogs pa skye mched re re ba'i dngos po dang, bum pa la sogs pa rang gi cha shas kyi dngos po tshogs pa gang yang zhig pa de'i mtshan gzhir mi rung ba'i phyir dngos po min no snyam pa'o
rows.english: According to the first of these two positions, when a functional thing like a sprout comes to an end, all the functional entities which constitute component parts of the sprout are cancelled. At the same time, no entity other than the sprout—nothing like a water pitcher or the like—is thus actualized; and, as such, they have to say that there cannot be the slightest functional thing left here. What they are thinking is that there is nothing at all that would be fitting to point to as a classical example of this kind of stopping—neither the functional things represented by the individual doors of sense such as blue or the like; nor functioning things which are conglomerates of their components, as in the case of pitchers or the like. As such, they would say, the stopping could never itself be a functional thing.

rows.wylie: chu klung gi rgyun ltar rgyun chags par rgyu dang 'bras bu 'brel bar 'jug pa na, skye 'chi brgyud pas bar stong med par rnam par ma chad par gnas pa, 'du byed kyi skad cig dus gsum pa'i nye bar len pa can la bya ste, skad cig ma rnams gang gi cha shas yin pa'i cha can yin gyi snga phyi bar ma chad pa tsam min no
rows.english: And so suppose we have causes and their effects going on in a connection, in a continued series which resembles the flow of a stream of fresh water. As such, a flow of birth and death goes on with a single break inbetween, uninterrupted. The moments of fresh karma take as their precursor the object across the three times; it is the whole which possesses the moments as its parts; but then again it's not as if there is no disconnect between the moments, earlier & later.

rows.english: It is not though the case that, from the time it first started, the glass of water came with the three different parts, or that they stay with the glass of water until it eventually ends. What happens is that one of the parts of the glass filled with wet and flowing water provides a material cause, and the karma of the craving spirit provides a contributing factor; and then based on both of these the later continuation of one part of the glass of water starts being blood and pus.

rows.wylie: de'i tshe na brlan zhing gsher ba chu phor pa gang po de cha shas gsum ldan du yod kyang, gsum gas gsum ga mthong ba ma yin te yi dwags kyi las ngan pa bsags pa'i, dbang gis rnag khrag tu mthong dngos po gzhan gnyis ma mthong ba dang de bzhin du 'gro ba 'og ma gnyis la yang shes par bya ba yin pa'i phyir
rows.english: At this point, the glass full of wet and flowing water is something with three different parts. Nonetheless, it is not the case that all three different beings see all three parts. The craving spirit is forced by the bad karma he has collected to see the glass of water as pus and blood; and he doesn't see the other two things. One should understand that a similar case holds with the latter two types of beings.

rows.english: Another example would be the moon in springtime; one part of the feel of its rays on the body provides the material cause, and then the karma of a craving spirit provides a contributing factor. Based on these two, the spirit gets a sensation of heat, which is experienced by the consciousness of the body. So too with the wintertime sun; one part of the feel of its rays on the body provides the material cause, and then the karma of the craving spirit provides a contributing factor. Based on these two, the spirit gets a sensation cold, which is experienced by the consciousness of the body.

rows.english: Something can be the word of a Buddha, and not necessarily have to be spoken from his or her holy lips. The secret teachings of the White Parasol, for example, issued from the crest upon the Buddha's head. And not only that—all the different parts of a Buddha's body also have the ability to grant teachings: the instruction can come from the sacred hair on his or her forehead; from the front of their throat; from their ears; and even from their anus or other places. The teachings of the Buddha can even come from the sound of the trees of the forest, blowing in the wind.

rows.acip: RTEN 'BREL YIN PA'I DON YANG RANG GI CHA SHAS SOGS LA BLTOS PA'I DON YIN PAS, CHOS THAMS CAD KYANG RANG RANG GI CHA SHAS SOGS LA BLTOS PA YIN LA CHA SHAS LA MA BLTOS PA NI MED DE, NAM MKHA'I ME TOG BZHIN NO ZHES BYA BAR DGONGS SO,,

rows.english: And what does it mean when we say that “things exist in dependence”? It means that all of them rely upon their parts, and so on. That is, everything in the universe depends upon its own particular parts and so on: there is nothing that doesn't rely on its parts. And that's why Je Tsongkapa's verse here says that such a thing would be “like a flower blossoming in thin air.”

rows.acip: CHOS THAMS CAD RTOG PAS BTAGS PA'I DPE NI, THAG PA KHRA BO YUL MI GSAL BA NA GNAS PA'I TSE KHA CIG LA 'DI SBRUL LO SNYAM PA'I BLO 'BYUNG NGO, ,DE'I TSE THAG PA DE'I TSOGS PA DANG CHA SHAS GANG YANG SBRUL DU MED KYANG, DE LA SBRUL LO SNYAM PA'I SBRUL NI RTOG PAS BTAGS PA TZAM DU 'CHAR RO,,
rows.wylie: chos thams cad rtog pas btags pa'i dpe ni, thag pa khra bo yul mi gsal ba na gnas pa'i tshe kha cig la 'di sbrul lo snyam pa'i blo 'byung ngo, ,de'i tshe thag pa de'i tshogs pa dang cha shas gang yang sbrul du med kyang, de la sbrul lo snyam pa'i sbrul ni rtog pas btags pa tsam du 'char ro
rows.english: There is a metaphor used to describe how all existing things are labeled with our concepts. When you put a rope with a checkered pattern on it in a dark corner, some people might get the impression that it's a snake. The truth at this point though is that nothing about the rope is a snake: neither the rope as a whole, nor the parts of the rope. Nonetheless the person thinks of the rope as a snake, and this snake is an example of something which only makes its appearance as something labeled with a concept.

rows.acip: DE BZHIN DU PHUNG PO 'DI LA BRTEN NAS NGA'O SNYAM DU 'BYUNG YANG, PHUNG PO'I TSOGS PA DANG RGYUN DANG CHA SHAS GANG YANG NGA'I MTSAN GZHIR 'JOG RGYU MED CING, PHUNG PO LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA GZHAN ZHIG KYANG NGA'I MTSAN GZHIR BZUNG MED PAS, NGA DE NI PHUNG PO LA BRTEN NAS BTAGS PA TZAM YIN GYI, RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA MED DO,,
rows.wylie: de bzhin du phung po 'di la brten nas nga'o snyam du 'byung yang, phung po'i tshogs pa dang rgyun dang cha shas gang yang nga'i mtshan gzhir 'jog rgyu med cing, phung po las ngo bo tha dad pa gzhan zhig kyang nga'i mtshan gzhir bzung med pas, nga de ni phung po la brten nas btags pa tsam yin gyi, rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa med do
rows.english: In the same way, the heaps of parts that make us up serve as a basis for us to get the impression “This is me.” There is nothing at all about these heaps as a whole, nor their continuation over time, nor their separate components, that we could establish as being an actual representation of “me.” At the same time though there is nothing else, nothing essentially separate from these heaps of parts to ourselves, that we could consider an actual representation of “me” either. As such, this “me” is merely something labeled upon the heaps of parts that make us up; there is nothing which exists by its own essence.

rows.english: The part of the verse that goes from “not earth” up to “not consciousness” is meant to deny that you could ever establish a self-nature of the person in any of the six elements that make up a persona, considered separately. The final line of the verse denies that there could be any self-nature which was essentially separate from these same elements.

rows.wylie: on kyang ma brtag ma dpyad pa'i blo ngo na yod pas tha snyad du zhing gi bkod pa rnams zhes bya'o, ,sangs rgyas kyi zhing du ma zad, snod bcud kyi bkod pa thams cad kyang cha shas du ma tshogs pa la btags pa ste, khang pa la sogs pa bzhin no, ,de dag thams cad kyang rigs pas rdul phra rab kyi bar bshig na ci yang ma yin pa'i bar 'gyur te mtshon tsam mo
rows.english: Since though they do exist to that state of mind which performs no check or analysis, we can nominally call them “paradise.” This fact refers not only to the paradise of a Buddha, but also to each and every thing which has ever been put here: to both the world where beings live, and to the beings who live in the world. All of these are simply a label put on the collection of a number of parts: they are all the same as a house, for example. And all of these are such that, should you break them down mentally all the way to their tiniest atoms, you would reach the point where they are nothing at all. (This is the briefest sketch of the meaning for you.)

rows.english: Now admittedly all the elements listed here are metaphorical; but we can say that “part” refers to greater or lesser components. “Countable” means this many more or less; “example” is a reference to different illustrations. “No comparison” is to say that nothing is its equal; “reason” refers to all the various ones you could think of; and “putting in numbers” means finding a number that could equal the amount of merit—and none of these ever could.

rows.wylie: chos thams cad rtog pas btags pa'i dpe ni, thag pa khra bo yul mi gsal ba na gnas pa'i tshe kha cig la 'di sbrul lo snyam pa'i blo 'byung ngo, ,de'i tshe thag pa de'i tshogs pa dang cha shas gang yang sbrul du med kyang, de la sbrul lo snyam pa'i sbrul ni rtog pas btags pa tsam du 'char ro
rows.english: There is a metaphor used to describe how all existing things are labeled with our concepts. When you put a rope with a checkered pattern on it in a dark corner, some people might get the impression that it's a snake. The truth at this point though is that nothing about the rope is a snake: neither the rope as a whole, nor the parts of the rope. Nonetheless the person thinks of the rope as a snake, and this snake is an example of something which only makes its appearance as something labeled with a concept.

rows.acip: DE BZHIN DU PHUNG PO 'DI LA BRTEN NAS NGA'O SNYAM DU 'BYUNG YANG, PHUNG PO'I TSOGS PA DANG RGYUN DANG CHA SHAS GANG YANG NGA'I MTSAN GZHIR 'JOG RGYU MED CING, PHUNG PO LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA GZHAN ZHIG KYANG NGA'I MTSAN GZHIR BZUNG MED PAS, NGA DE NI PHUNG PO LA BRTEN NAS BTAGS PA TZAM YIN GYI, RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA MED DO,,
rows.wylie: de bzhin du phung po 'di la brten nas nga'o snyam du 'byung yang, phung po'i tshogs pa dang rgyun dang cha shas gang yang nga'i mtshan gzhir 'jog rgyu med cing, phung po las ngo bo tha dad pa gzhan zhig kyang nga'i mtshan gzhir bzung med pas, nga de ni phung po la brten nas btags pa tsam yin gyi, rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa med do
rows.english: In the same way, the heaps of parts that make us up serve as a basis for us to get the impression "This is me." There is nothing at all about these heaps as a whole, nor their continuation over time, nor their separate components, that we could establish as being an actual representation of "me." At the same time though there is nothing else, nothing essentially separate from these heaps of parts to ourselves, that we could consider an actual representation of "me" either. As such, this "me" is merely something labeled upon the heaps of parts that make us up; there is nothing which exists by its own essence.

rows.english: The part of the verse that goes from "not earth" up to "not consciousness" is meant to deny that you could ever establish a self-nature of the person in any of the six elements that make up a persona, considered separately. The words "not all of them" are meant to deny that you could establish such a self-nature in the collection of the six elements, considered as a whole. The final line of the verse denies that there could be any self-nature which was essentially separate from these same elements.

rows.wylie: on kyang ma brtag ma dpyad pa'i blo ngo na yod pas tha snyad du zhing gi bkod pa rnams zhes bya'o, ,sangs rgyas kyi zhing du ma zad, snod bcud kyi bkod pa thams cad kyang cha shas du ma tshogs pa la btags pa ste, khang pa la sogs pa bzhin no, ,de dag thams cad kyang rigs pas rdul phra rab kyi bar bshig na ci yang ma yin pa'i bar 'gyur te mtshon tsam
rows.english: MO,,Since though they do exist to that state of mind which performs no check or analysis, we can nominally call them "paradise." This fact refers not only to the paradise of a Buddha, but also to each and every thing which has ever been put here: to both the world where beings live, and to the beings who live in the world. All of these are simply a label put on the collection of a number of parts: they are all the same as a house, for example. And all of these are such that, should you break them down mentally all the way to their tiniest atoms, you would reach the point where they are nothing at all. (This is the briefest sketch of the meaning for you.)

rows.english: Now admittedly all the elements listed here are metaphorical; but we can say that "part" refers to greater or lesser components. "Countable" means this many more or less; "example" is a reference to different illustrations. "No comparison" is to say that nothing is its equal; "reason" refers to all the various ones you could think of; and "putting in numbers" means finding a number that could equal the amount of merit—and none of these ever could.

rows.acip: DE YANG BLO PHYI MA DE SHUGS CHES NA BLO SNGA MA DE YAL NAS STONG SANG ZHIG MA GTOGS GANG YANG MI YONG BAS SHES PA BYINGS NGA'O SNYAM PA'I BLO DE'I NGO BOR BRENG CHAGS SU BSKYED NAS, SHES PA'I CHA SHAS PHRA MO ZHIG GIS BRTAG DGOS LA,
rows.wylie: de yang blo phyi ma de shugs ches na blo snga ma de yal nas stong sang zhig ma gtogs gang yang mi yong bas shes pa byings nga'o snyam pa'i blo de'i ngo bor breng chags su bskyed nas, shes pa'i cha shas phra mo zhig gis brtag dgos la
rows.english: Now it may happen that the second part of the mind may get too strong: and then the first part of it will just disappear into thin air.  If this happens you won't get anywhere, just some sensation of something lost.  It's crucial therefore that you maintain this little side section of you mind to observe what's going on, even in the face of that constant stream of the part of your mind which is thinking me, me, at its deepest levels.

rows.acip: DAM PA RIGS BRGYA NI, PHUNG PO LNGA, KHAMS BZHI, MIG SOGS SKYE MCHED DRUG, GZUGS SGRA SOGS LNGA STE RAGS PA NYI SHU LA CHA SHAS LNGA LNGAR PHYE STE, GSHEGS PA LNGA, YUM BZHI, SA SNYING SOGS SEMS DPA' DRUG ,GZUGS RDO RJE MA SOGS LNGA STE LHA NYI SHU LA RIGS LNGA LNGAR PHYE STE SGOM PA'O,,
rows.wylie: dam pa rigs brgya ni, phung po lnga, khams bzhi, mig sogs skye mched drug, gzugs sgra sogs lnga ste rags pa nyi shu la cha shas lnga lngar phye ste, gshegs pa lnga, yum bzhi, sa snying sogs sems dpa' drug ,gzugs rdo rje ma sogs lnga ste lha nyi shu la rigs lnga lngar phye ste sgom pa'o
rows.english: The hundred classes of the ultimate are meditating upon the following things.  We first take twenty gross objects--the five heaps; the four categories; the six sense gateways of the eye and the rest; and the five of visible forms, sounds, and so on.  We then divide these five groups into five others: the Five Enlightened Ones; the Four Holy Women; the Six Bodhisattvas, the ones known as Essence of the Earth and the rest; and the five of the Diamond Lady of Forms and the others.  These twenty are then divided up into five each--corresponding to the Five Families--which makes a total of a hundred.

rows.acip: MDOR NA BDE MCHOG LHA DRUG CU RE GNYIS RTEN DANG BRTEN PAR BCAS PA KHA tV'Am GA LA TSANG ZHING, DE THAMS CAD KYANG GTZO BO LAS RGYUD THA DAD PA MA YIN GYI GTZO BO'I YE SHES KHO NA'I CHA SHAS LAS GRUB PAS DE'I RNAM 'GYUR YIN PAS NA YAB MTSON ZHING SBAS PA'I TSUL GYIS 'DZIN PA'O, ,
rows.wylie: mdor na bde mchog lha drug cu re gnyis rten dang brten par bcas pa kha TvAM ga la tshang zhing, de thams cad kyang gtso bo las rgyud tha dad pa ma yin gyi gtso bo'i ye shes kho na'i cha shas las grub pas de'i rnam 'gyur yin pas na yab mtshon zhing sbas pa'i tshul gyis 'dzin pa'o,
rows.english: To put it briefly, the entire secret world of Highest Bliss--the 62 beings and the places where they stay--are all complete in this khatvanga.  None of these beings is a separate person from the central figure, but rather they are literally made of nothing more than a piece of His wisdom--and are thus His expression.  And so the staff represents the Man, and She holds Him in a way which is hidden from others.

rows.acip: LUS LA LHA BSGOM PA TZAM GYIS LUS DKYIL MA YIN TE, DPER NA SKYE MCHED BZHIN YIN PAR GSUNGS KYANG, SA DGE'I YIG CHA PHAL MO CHER MA THON PA MAN NGAG LA YOD SHAG DANG, RANG GI LUS KYI CHA SHAS KYIS LHAN CIG BYED PA'I RKYEN DANG, SNGAGS PHRENG GIS NYE BAR LEN PA'I RGYU BYAS PA LA BRTEN NAS 'BYUNG BA YIN TE,
rows.wylie: lus la lha bsgom pa tsam gyis lus dkyil ma yin te, dper na skye mched bzhin yin par gsungs kyang, sa dge'i yig cha phal mo cher ma thon pa man ngag la yod shag dang, rang gi lus kyi cha shas kyis lhan cig byed pa'i rkyen dang, sngags phreng gis nye bar len pa'i rgyu byas pa la brten nas 'byung ba yin te
rows.english: It is not the case that something is the practice of the secret world of the body just because you visualize Angels inside of your body.  For example, some people have said that the secret world of the body is important simply because you use the physical parts of your body.  Although the majority of both the Sakya tradition and the Way of the Pure fail to bring out the reason why this practice is so profound, the point is made in the oral advices of our Lamas.  The secret world of the body arises from the contributing factor of the various parts of your own body, and the material cause of the string of secret words.

rows.acip: 'O NA JI LTAR YIN ZHE NA, RANG RDO RJE 'CHANG DU GNAS PA DE LAS THA MAL PA'I LUS KYI CHA SHAS RE CHAD NAS THIM PAS GZHAL YAS KHANG SKAD CIG GI SNGA MA DES NYE BAR LEN PA'I RGYU DANG, SKAD CIG PHYI MA RANG GI LUS DES LHAN CIG BYED PA'I RKYEN BYAS NAS GRUB PA LTAR RO,
rows.wylie: 'o na ji ltar yin zhe na, rang rdo rje 'chang du gnas pa de las tha mal pa'i lus kyi cha shas re chad nas thim pas gzhal yas khang skad cig gi snga ma des nye bar len pa'i rgyu dang, skad cig phyi ma rang gi lus des lhan cig byed pa'i rkyen byas nas grub pa ltar ro
rows.english: How then are we supposed to do this practice?  Hold your visualization of yourself as the Keeper of the Diamond, and then imagine that pieces from the channels of your normal body break off and then sink into the crystal palace at your heart.  The first instant of the palace provides the material cause, and in the next instant comes a piece of your body that provides the contributing factor, for the mandala.

rows.acip: SGRUB GZHI RANG GI LUS KYI CHA SHAS LAS GRUB PA'AM, LUS KYI CHA SHAS LA BRTEN NAS BSKYED PA'I DKYIL 'KHOR LA LUS DKYIL ZHES BYA,
rows.wylie: sgrub gzhi rang gi lus kyi cha shas las grub pa'am, lus kyi cha shas la brten nas bskyed pa'i dkyil 'khor la lus dkyil zhes bya
rows.english: Here the basic material is our body: the secret world is made of parts of our body, or you can say created using the various parts of the body.  And so we call it the "secret world of the body."

rows.acip: CHA SHAS RE CHAD DE THIM PA YONGS SU GYUR PA LAS 'KHOR LO GSUM GYI DPA' MO NYER BZHI BSKYED,

From these arise the twenty-four woman Warriors of the three groups relating to holy body, speech, and mind.

rows.acip: LUS DKYIL BSGOM SKABS BLO'I PHYOGS GCIG NAS RNAL 'BYOR MA SO BDUN PO RNAMS SGRUB GZHI RANG GI LUS KYI CHA SHAS RTZA KHAMS RNAMS LAS GRUB PAS RTZA KHAMS DE DANG DE DNGOS YIN SNYAM PA DGOS, DE MED NA LUS DKYIL DU MI 'GRO,
rows.wylie: lus dkyil bsgom skabs blo'i phyogs gcig nas rnal 'byor ma so bdun po rnams sgrub gzhi rang gi lus kyi cha shas rtsa khams rnams las grub pas rtsa khams de dang de dngos yin snyam pa dgos, de med na lus dkyil du mi 'gro
rows.english: While you are actually performing the meditation of the secret world of your body, part of your mind has to focus on the thirty- seven Angels and think how they are in reality this or that channel and substance, since they are made of different parts of your body, having come forth from the various channels and substances.  If this step is missing, then the practice is not one of the secret world of the body.

rows.english: We need to think to ourselves that these are the actual Angels of Diamond and Warriors who live in the 37 places: the 24 sacred sites, the eight burial grounds, the four continents, and the great mountain. rows.acip: DE LA YANG GNYIS LAS RNAM PA LA BSLAB PA NI, LHA DE'I RNAM PA YAS RIM MAM, MAS RIM NAS SKU'I CHA SHAS RAGS PA CIG GSAL GDAB LA, YID NGOR CHA PHYED PA LAM ME BA CIG 'CHAR THUB PA DANG, DE GA LA SEMS GRIMS LHOD RAN PAR RTZE GCIG TU BZHAG ,
rows.wylie: de la yang gnyis las rnam pa la bslab pa ni, lha de'i rnam pa yas rim mam, mas rim nas sku'i cha shas rags pa cig gsal gdab la, yid ngor cha phyed pa lam me ba cig 'char thub pa dang, de ga la sems grims lhod ran par rtse gcig tu bzhag
rows.english: There are two steps to this focussing of the mind; here is how you train yourself in the physical appearance of the figure.  Pull up the appearance of the Angel, starting either from the top or the bottom, focussing on some obvious section of Their body.  Keep up on this section until you are able to get the part to appear bright and clear in your mind.  Then concentrate your mind on this same spot, adjusting the tightness of the concentration until you get it just right.

rows.acip: RO RKYANG DBU MA GSUM GYI YAR SNE LUS KYI DBUS DRANGS THAD NAS SONG STE RTZE MO CUNG ZAD GUG NAS SMIN DBUS KYI NANG THAD DANG G-YAS G-YON DU GNAS SHING MAR SNA SKYES PA LA RTAGS KYI RTZE DANG BUD MED LA PAD+MA'I RTZER ZUG STE GNAS YANG , CHA SHAS RE RKANG MTHIL GYI BAR DU YOD DO,,
rows.wylie: ro rkyang dbu ma gsum gyi yar sne lus kyi dbus drangs thad nas song ste rtse mo cung zad gug nas smin dbus kyi nang thad dang g-yas g-yon du gnas shing mar sna skyes pa la rtags kyi rtse dang bud med la pad+ma'i rtser zug ste gnas yang , cha shas re rkang mthil gyi bar du yod do
rows.english: The upper ends of these three channels--the channel of taste, the solitary channel, and the central channel--extend straight up through the middle of the body; then the tip bends down a bit until it reaches the level of the spot between the eyebrows, where they then go down a little to the right and left. The lower ends of the same channels, in a male, extend down to the tip of the penis; in a female, to the tip of the vagina.  There are also parts of these channels that extend down to the soles of the two feet.

rows.acip: RO MA'I NANG NAS KHAMS DMAR PO DANG , RKYANG MA'I NANG NAS KHAMS DKAR PO 'BAB PAR GSUNGS PA NI GTZO BO'I DBANG DU BYAS PA YIN GYI, GZHAN DU NA GNYIS KA'I NANG NAS KHU KHRAG 'BAB PA YIN TE, KHAMS DKAR PO LA KHRAG GI CHA SHAS 'JUG CING , LAM DUS SU RTZA STONG PHRAG DON GNYIS NAS KYANG BYANG SEMS 'BAB PAR BSHAD PA'I PHYIR RO,
rows.wylie: ro ma'i nang nas khams dmar po dang , rkyang ma'i nang nas khams dkar po 'bab par gsungs pa ni gtso bo'i dbang du byas pa yin gyi, gzhan du na gnyis ka'i nang nas khu khrag 'bab pa yin te, khams dkar po la khrag gi cha shas 'jug cing , lam dus su rtsa stong phrag don gnyis nas kyang byang sems 'bab par bshad pa'i phyir ro
rows.english: Now the scriptures state that the red element flows through the channel of taste, and that the white element flows through the solitary channel.  This only means though that these are what primarily flow through these channels.  This is because, in addition, both the semen and blood elements flow through both channels: it is stated that a certain amount of the white element comes in the blood element, and that--for a person practicing the path--the element of enlightenment flows through all 72,000 channels. Our Inner Knots, the Chakras The following translation is an excerpt from Je Tsongkapa's famous Commentary on the Practice of the Diamond Recitation, which can be found in the ACIP database, text S5292, folios 19B-20A. . *********** The Chakras and their Petals

rows.acip: DE YANG THOG MAR PHA MA'I RTEN 'BREL DANG, RANG GI SEMS LA LAS KYI BAG CHAGS BSGOS PA'I MTHUS, MI LUS GRUB PA'I DUS SU DANG POR LTE BAR KUN 'DAR GYI CHA SHAS PHRA BRENG BA CIG CHAGS TE, DE LA AA NA HA DA ZHES BYA'O,,
rows.wylie: de yang thog mar pha ma'i rten 'brel dang, rang gi sems la las kyi bag chags bsgos pa'i mthus, mi lus grub pa'i dus su dang por lte bar kun 'dar gyi cha shas phra breng ba cig chags te, de la aa na ha da zhes bya'o
rows.english: Now at the beginning, as a human body first forms, something grows at the navel, due to the interaction of the parents and the power of karmic seeds infused previously in the mind.  This is a very fine, elongated section of the trembling channel, and it is given the name of anahada,

rows.acip: DE'I STENG DU (NYI) MA DANG (ZLA) BA CHA SHAS (RGYAS PA) STE NYA GANG BA('I) GDAN RNAMS KYI (STENG) DU SGOM PAR BYED PA YIN NO,,
rows.wylie: de'i steng du (nyi) ma dang (zla) ba cha shas (rgyas pa) ste nya gang ba('i) gdan rnams kyi (steng) du sgom par byed pa yin no
rows.english: Atop the lotus are cushions of full circles of the sun and the moon--referring to the appearance that the latter for example has when it is full.  And it is upon them that we will be visualizing our Lama.

rows.acip: GZHAN YANG DE'I CHA SHAS ('JIG RTEN) NI SO SO SKYE BO DANG, ('JIG RTEN LAS 'DAS) PA 'PHAGS PA RNAMS TE MDOR NA (RANG) DANG (GZHAN GYI) LUS NGAG YID KYI (SGO GSUM) DU BSAGS PA'I (DGE BA'I ME TOG) GI TSOGS LTA BU (CI YANG BKRA) BA STE SNA TSOGS PA CIR YANG MDZES PAR SNANG BA DANG,
rows.wylie: gzhan yang de'i cha shas ('jig rten) ni so so skye bo dang, ('jig rten las 'das) pa 'phags pa rnams te mdor na (rang) dang (gzhan gyi) lus ngag yid kyi (sgo gsum) du bsags pa'i (dge ba'i me tog) gi tshogs lta bu (ci yang bkra) ba ste sna tshogs pa cir yang mdzes par snang ba dang
rows.english: And this goodness can as well be divided into that of this world--that is, that accomplished by normal beings--and that which is beyond this world: accomplished by realized beings.  In brief then we are offering the flowers of the goodness which have been accumulated much like bouquets by both myself and others, through our three doors of expression: in acts and words and thoughts.  And this goodness is shining, in the sense that it is beautiful to behold, in all its lovely variety.
